interpretation: The seven weak selected profiles have positive fixed-channel averages with13–16 positive center-minus-flank rows in their originating ON scans. Their excesses have temporal distribution within the existing data; they are not automatically attributable to one integration.

ON2 rank1 provides the clearest fixed-channel sign persistence among these seven selected profiles. The 16 positive signs cannot be used as an unconditioned binomial test because the channel was selected using the same time-averaged data.

These are seven post-selected ON excesses, not seven independently confirmed transmitters or observing visits. Different frequencies in the same historical sequence do not supply independent sky followup.
The fixed-channel time profiles and waterfalls inspect the same powers used for spectral selection. They reveal temporal morphology but supply no independent statistical confirmation.
Fractional spectral contrast and center-minus-flank power use different normalizations/background definitions; their numerical magnitudes are not interchangeable.
The shared clipped waterfall scale can obscure weak spectral structure. Lack of an obvious visual continuous line does not establish a noise origin.
All seven are retained as unresolved. The existing failures and lack of qualified sky sensitivity remain unchanged.
